articleTitle: Optimal Electric Bus Charging Scheduling for Local Balancing of Fluctuations in PV Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Photovoltaic power generation and charging of electric vehicles each pose a burden to distribution grids. Controlled charging of electric vehicles can mitigate the fluctuations of photovoltaics and ensure smoother grid operation. This paper presents an optimisation method to adjust the charging power of electric buses to respond to fluctuations from photovoltaic generation. In a case study, the method is applied to electric buses in Singapore using solar irradiance data and operation data of the whole public bus fleet, both in high resolution. Results show that optimal charging of electric public buses considerably smooths the grid load, while leading only to a minor cost increase.

articleTitle: Synchrophasor Measurements for Power System Monitoring and Control under the Standard IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Synchrophasor measurement was first introduced in the 1980's and has proven to be indispensable to the analysis and understanding of wide area grid dynamics. It has also proven to be crucial to monitor and control of the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources. Firstly this paper briefs the history of standard development from IEEE 1344 to recently issued IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1. Then this paper describes the changes from the previous IEEE standards, such as modification of several definitions for greater clarity, testing simplification, higher precision accuracy qualification and full bandwidth determination. This paper further discusses two classes of performance (P class and M class) defined in the standard, and points out that the users need to consider the compromise between the interrelated factors. Different applications for power grid monitoring and control need careful selection of performance class introduced in the standard. Finally, this paper discusses the further standard development in the area of digitalized sampling value input and future application for distribution level grid.

articleTitle: Tech-economic Benefit Evaluation and Decision for Distribution Network Planning Based on Fuzzy Analysis Hierarchical Process
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Investment benefit evaluation for the distribution network is the important basis for distribution network planning and reconstruction. This paper initial on a comprehensive benefit index framework for distribution network from extensive literature. This framework is constructed from two aspects of technical characteristics and economic benefit, so-called tech-economic benefits index framework. It is important for guiding precise investment to research a set of reasonable and comprehensive evaluation model for plan and reform investment of distribution network. Comparison of index results for different planning schemes are given, including (distribution generations) DGs, switches, feeder lines, etc. A comprehensive evaluation method is put forward to analysis the optimal scheme based on improved fuzzy hierarchical analysis method. And a correlative investment decision model is presented. The planning objective is to maximize the social benefits of the whole system. On the basis, comprehensive economic-benefit evaluation is verified and demonstrated by test cases, the optimal plan and the analysis is also implemented.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Energy Hubs in an Integrated Energy System Considering Contingencies in Critical Branches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: An energy hub (EH), acting as an energy receiving, converting and storing unit, is one of the most important components in an integrated energy system (IES). How to properly determine the optimal configuration of components in an EH is an important issue with extensive concerns, and is the subject of this work. A mixed integer linear programming model is presented for this purpose. In order to ensure reliable energy supply under bad operating conditions, credible contingencies in some critical branches in the IES are considered in formulating the optimal design problem. Three indexes are then presented, including the line betweenness, the connection importance and the maximum transmission capability, to evaluate the overall importance degree of each branch. An entropy weight method is next adopted to determine the evaluation weight of each index. Finally, a sample IES is employed to demonstrate the feasibility and efficiency of the presented method.

articleTitle: A P2P Trading Mechanism of Distributed PV Based on Continuous Matching
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Energy crisis and environmental pollution have drawn lots of attentions to the development of renewable energy. As a clean renewable energy source, photovoltaics (PV) generation has been experiencing a dramatic growth worldwide. Aiming at the accelerate trading of distributed PV in the electricity market, this paper proposes a P2P distributed PV day-ahead market trading mechanism based on continuous matching. In addition, an optimal bidding strategy is developed based on a bidding tendency model to maximize trading benefits. Numerical results show that the transaction architecture and mechanism can promote the consumption of photovoltaic energy among peers, and effectively improve the transaction profit of peers.

articleTitle: BP Neural Network Based Fault Prediction of Distribution Network during Typhoon Disaster
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Typhoon disasters will cause faults such as reversing, disconnection, wind flashover, etc., which threaten the safe and reliable operation of the distribution network. It is necessary to predict the failure of the distribution network caused by typhoon disasters. Considering that a large number of historical data from typhoon and distribution network fault information are retained in the meteorological information acquisition system, it is very suitable to use artificial neural network to explore the correlation between meteorological information and distribution network fault information. Therefore, this paper proposes a fault prediction model of distribution tower during typhoon disaster based on BP neural network. The fault prediction model of distribution network based on BP neural network is established firstly. Then the parameters in the model are optimized by training samples. Lastly, the validity of model prediction is tested by test samples. The test results show that the proposed method can accurately predict the fault trip of the distribution network tower during typhoon disasters.

articleTitle: Integrated Flexible Resources and Energy Markets in the Danish Multi-energy System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The core concept of the multi-energy system (MES) brings new insights for flexible resources. Integrated flexible resources (IFR) and the ancillary integrated energy market (IEM) become critical and effective measures to ensure reliable and flexible operation of the future MES. This paper firstly introduces the basic concept and the benefits of IFR. The existing status and future energy markets integration in Denmark are then summarized. Finally, the research opportunities of IFR and the IEM in the MES are proposed.

articleTitle: Planning of Distributed Energy Resources in Singapore
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To aid in the reduction of the dependency on fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions that cause poor air quality, migration from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to electric vehicles (EV) is advised. It will also be essential to integrate renewable energy sources (RES) like photovoltaics (PVs), wind, biogas etc. However, there is little progress in Singapore due to the limited EV electric range in affordable EVs and low EV charging availability. Hence, there is a need for EV charging stations (EV CS) implementation to ease anxiety range, without causing adverse effects on existing electric distribution networks. In this paper, siting and sizing of EV CS is done using K-means clustering algorithm on a test feeder with various predicted EV penetration levels applicable to Singapore. Linear approximation on complex plane power flow analysis and cost analysis were implemented to check the practicality of the proposed methodology. The results showed feasibility in the three EV penetration levels of low 10%, medium 30%, and high 50% with AC slow charging. Optimal charging device rating is AC slow 3.3 kW to better meet the potential charging demands of private vehicles in Singapore, which are to be implemented in residential car parking areas.

articleTitle: BIRCH Algorithm and Wasserstein Distance Metric Based Method for Generating Typical Scenarios of Wind Power Outputs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the ever-increasing penetration of renewable energy generation such as wind power and solar photovoltaics, the power system concerned is suffering more extensive and significant uncertainties. Scenario analysis has been utilized to solve this problem for power system planning and operation, but heavy computation burden is involved especially for large-scale power systems. To better address this problem, an algorithm based on the BIRCH (Balanced Iterative Reducing and Clustering using Hierarchies) algorithm and Wasserstein distance metrics is proposed in this paper to reduce the scenarios of wind power outputs. First, the Wasserstein distance is employed to attain the optimal quantiles for discretizing the continuous density function of wind power outputs. Then, the BIRCH algorithm, which is suitable for large volume of data, is utilized to determine the typical scenarios. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through case studies and comparisons with some existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimized Planning of P2G Plant in Integrated Electricity and Natural Gas System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The wind resource is comparatively abundant and the installed capacity of wind power in some areas has increased rapidly in recent years, but the phenomenon of the curtailment of wind power under high penetration is still serious. Power-to-gas (P2G) can be used as a large-scale storage device to store the excess wind power. In this paper, an optimal planning strategy for integrated electricity and natural gas system by means of particle swarm optimization (PSO) is proposed, the P2G devices are added in this hybrid system. The goal of this strategy is to optimize the sizing of P2G plant based on return on investment (ROI) index. The results show that the optimal sizing of P2G plant is 92.43 MW which can reduce about 70% excess wind power, and the ROI is 16.45 years.

articleTitle: Impact of Utility-Scale Energy Storage Systems on Power System Transient Stability Considering Operating Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the improvement in energy storage and power electronic control technologies, utility-scale energy storage systems (ESS) have been increasingly deployed in today's power systems and have shown great potential in providing ancillary services. This paper investigates the impact of ESSs on power system transient stability in the context of uncertainties from renewable generation and demand-side activities. The transient behavior of ESSs with varying battery charging/discharging characteristics is first investigated, and trajectory sensitivity analysis is then performed to quantify the sensitivity of ESS parameters on post-disturbance rotor angle development. The case study was performed on a wind-penetrated power system with industrial-grade dynamic BESS models.

articleTitle: Dynamic Conductor Temperature Modelling and Analysis of a Distribution Network with PV
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The IEEE Std 1283™-2013 details the adverse effects of high conductor temperatures, which emphasises the need to model and analyse dynamic conductor temperatures in a power network. Conductor temperatures are dependent on the power flows (due to load current), the resistive losses, and the weather conditions surrounding the conductor. Conventional power system analysis does not take into account changing weather and its impacts and as a result, studies conducted are erroneous due to absence of such realistic assumptions of the weather impacts. In this manuscript, a dynamic conductor temperature model is presented and utilised to study and thermally profile the conductor temperatures in a distribution network. The proposed approach is decoupled i.e. the power flow and the conductor heat balance model are solved separately to obtain the thermal profile network conductors in operation. In comparison to the existing approach suggested in the literature, the proposed approach is computational light and can be easily scaled to larger networks. Simulations were carried out for two cases with different load and weather conditions. The changing weather conditions and their impact on the network and thermal profile was understood by utilising the proposed technique. The simulation results presented show the advantages of using dynamic conductor temperature modelling in power system studies for better analysis of power networks.

articleTitle: Power Optimization Strategy for Typical Industrial Users under the Condition of Time-of-use Pricing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent electrical technologies and power demand response (DR), the power consumption scale of industrial users has expanded dramatically. Aiming at satisfying the diverse demands of industrial customers, the paper proposes three typical power optimization schemes for industrial users, which are all based on improved genetic algorithm (GA). Firstly, representative industrial load types and their corresponding demand response modes are put forward. Secondly, according to the respective demands of industrial users, a variety of power consumption models under time-of-use pricing are constructed and solved by improved genetic algorithm. Finally, the power optimization schemes proposed in the paper are verified by Matlab simulations. The results indicate that schemes designed by improved GA significantly outperform traditional GA schemes in terms of satisfying the industrial power demands over economy, efficiency and accuracy separately.

articleTitle: Complementarity Analysis and Evaluation of Renewable Energy Stations based on Mixed-Copula Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Multi-energy complementarity is an effective way to improve the utilization capacity for renewable energy sources in the grid. Correlation analyses on the power of different new energy units are the key to evaluating their complementary degree. Compared with traditional linear analytical methods, Copula functions can well capture the nonlinear tail correlation between random variables. In order to describe the complementary characteristics of renewable energy stations, this paper introduces the mixed-Copula theory to construct the two-dimensional dependence structure model of renewable energy output. A stochastic scenario generation method based on the acceptance-rejection sampling is proposed to simulate the power subject to the Copula correlation. In addition, combined with the conditional probability in the upper and lower tail intervals, a complementarity evaluation index is developed to describe the coupling degree of the power from different renewable energy plants. The comparison with the existing index verifies the effectiveness of the proposed evaluation method.

articleTitle: Short-term Optimized Operation of Multi-energy Power System Based on Complementary Characteristics of Power Sources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that uncertain power sources bring fluctuation to power system and cause lots of wind and photovoltaic curtailment, a short-term optimized operation method of multi-energy power system based on complementary characteristics of power sources is presented. The complementary mechanism of multi-energy power system is established. Based on the complementary mechanism, mathematical models of complementary objectives and complementary demands are established. Define renewable energy complementary power source. To minimize complementary demands, the capacity matching ratio of hydropower in renewable energy complementary power source is determined. According to the complementary objectives, a hierarchical optimal operation strategy for multi-energy power system is proposed. Particle swarm optimization is used to solve the optimization objective function. Taking a provincial power grid in northwest China as an example, the results show that the strategy makes full use of the complementarity of power sources and has the benefit of energy saving.

articleTitle: Study on 24h Dynamic Reactive Power Optimization Considering Safety Operation Limit of Generators
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In order to solve the practical problem of 24-hours dynamic reactive power optimization in power system dispatching, according to the limit output range of generator's operation, this paper divides generator's operation into three regions in PQ mathematical model and takes the action times of discrete control equipment as global inequality constraints, finally establishes a complete 24-hours non-linear mixed integer dynamic reactive power optimization mathematical model. The simulation results show that the mathematical model in this paper can adjust the output of the generators according to the actual situation effectively when the generators are in phase-leading operation. In addition, dynamic reactive power optimization reduces the number of control equipment's action at the cost of increasing active power loss in the whole network. So, In order to ensure the safe and economic operation of power grid, it is necessary to coordinate the relationship between active power loss and the constraints of control equipment's action. This paper has positive reference significance for power system dispatching.

articleTitle: Quanlitative and Quantitative Analysis on AC-Side Perturbation Characteristics of Voltage-Source Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To investigate the oscillation phenomenon caused by renewable energy integration, the ac-side perturbation characteristics of voltage-source converter (VSC) is studied qualitatively and quantitatively. Firstly, the propagation path of the ac-side perturbation in VSC is qualitatively analyzed. And the dq component asymmetry concept is introduced in the analyzing process, which illustrates the appearance of the complementary frequency perturbation component. Then, the quantitative relationship among the perturbation components in VSC is analyzed, specially considering the influence of the phase-locked loop (PLL). Finally, the port-impedance and the complementary frequency effect admittance of VSC are deduced, which are further verified by time-domain simulation. In addition, the influence of controller parameters on the port-impedance is also analyzed in the case study. It is concluded that the complementary frequency perturbation component is mainly caused by the PLL perturbation. And the PI parameters of PLL have a great influence on the port-impedance.

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Generation Expansion Planning Model Considering RES Integrations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: A generation expansion planning strategy to derive the optimal generation mix for distribution systems is proposed in this paper. The considered candidate units include decentralized storage units, variable generation units, dispatchable generation units and flexible loads. The uncertainties in demand, wind and PV generation forecasts are characterized by an ambiguity set that defines a family of distributions. Following the principle of distributionally robust optimization (DRO), a two-stage stochastic programming model is formulated to minimize the worst-case expectation of the sum of long-term investment costs and short-term operational costs. A case study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed model and the importance of considering more statistical characteristics of uncertain variables. The impacts of forecast errors' variances are analyzed and the results of using DRO with that of using robust optimization and stochastic optimization are compared.

articleTitle: Online Operation of Battery Energy Storage System for Demand Charge Reduction Considering Degradation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Online operation of the battery energy storage system (BESS) in industrial/commercial buildings suffers from the uncertainty of load forecasting. We propose an online model-free operation algorithm controlling charge/discharge of BESS for demand charge reduction with the consideration of battery degradation in this paper. We formulate the problem as an offline optimization problem first and then propose a Q-learning based algorithm to solve the real-time scheduling problem. The proposed method is and verified by actual building load data.

articleTitle: Marketing Models and Value-added Services of Power Grid Enterprises in Chinese Electricity Market Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The marketing of power grid enterprises has been facing unprecedented opportunities and challenges, brought by the reform of the power system and the construction of an energy internet environment ongoing in China. It is a pressing problem at present that what kind of marketing strategy should be adopted by power grid enterprises to enhance user stickiness and further expand the business of selling electricity. In this paper, the new marketing strategy of power grid enterprises in the energy internet environment is put forward from two aspects of the marketing model and the value-added service, based on the new situation and new demand brought by the reform of the power system. Firstly, the specific marketing model includes assisting large users to directly participate in market transactions, providing the service of electricity trading in the secondary market, and gradually establishing cultivation and service of the power spot market trading system for users. Secondly, value-added services are provided to users individually, or bundled with power sales services, the main purpose of which is to attract more users to choose the power grid enterprises as the main body of the electricity sale, so as to lock the market share and further create greater market revenue. Introduced marketing strategies can help power grid enterprises meet challenges and seize opportunities in the energy internet environment. By adjusting the marketing strategy, making a big market, expanding value-added service and attracting massive users, it can help the power grid enterprises to form the core competitiveness, grasp the initiative and realize the sustainable development.

articleTitle: Bi-level Demand Response Scheme in the Presence of Aggregators with Thermally Responsive Loads
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Demand response (DR) program is a cost-effective way to improve operation efficiency of distribution networks. Load aggregator (LA), as new market participant, has played active role in demand side management for pursuing profit. In this paper, we introduce a bi-level DR scheme for distribution network operating with a set of thermal LAs which group the distributed responsive end-users for win-win operation. The goal of the upper level is to optimize the revenue of utility operation. This model also ensures that thermal LAs are paid according to their contributions to economic improvements of distribution network. At lower level, LAs make optimal decision for dispatching the included thermal loads, while the latter decides whether accept the power shaving request for monetary subsidy by compromising the comfort experience. The simulation analysis indicate that the proposed bi-level DR scheme is able to fully leverage the responsive capability of thermal loads to enable distributed demand response. Meanwhile, the benefits of market stakeholders can be well balanced by providing them the flexible choices.

articleTitle: Wind Power Prediction Based on Principal Component Analysis and Long Short-Term Memory Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In recent years, the scale of new energy represented by wind power and photovoltaic has been continuously developed at a high speed. Due to the strong randomness and volatility of wind energy, it poses a severe challenge for the safety, reliability, stability and economy of grid operation. The effective improvement of wind power prediction accuracy is of great significance to power grid operation. Along with the continuous development of artificial intelligence methods, the emerging wind power prediction methods have been greatly improved in terms of prediction accuracy and calculation rate. As a current predictive model for deep learning, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is excellent for predicting long-term sequences. This paper proposes a wind power prediction method based on LSTM. In addition, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method is used to achieve the dimension reduction of data. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed PCA-LSTM method.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Accommodation Capability of a Distribution System for Electric Vehicles considering System Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The ever-increasing integration of distributed generation (DG) and numerous electric vehicles (EVs) into a power distribution system has imposed more uncertainties, and then operation flexibility is more demanded. It is necessary to quantitatively study the accommodation capability for EVs (ACE) by the power distribution system concerned so as to optimize the planning of EV infrastructures and the EV charging strategy, aiming at mitigating load fluctuations and maintaining system security. Given this background, the characteristics of flexible resources are introduced and two evaluation indices of the system flexibility proposed from the perspective of the system capacity and transmission capacity of the flexible resources. Next, an optimization model to evaluate the ACE by a distribution system with a high DG penetration level is established, considering optimal scheduling of the flexible resources, the physical operation constraints of the power system concerned, N-1 contingencies and the power shortage. The presented optimization model is a mixed integer programming problem, and solved by the combination of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm and the well-developed CPLEX solver. A modified version of the IEEE 118-node test system is served for demonstrating the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Real-time Dispatch with Flexible Ramping Products in a Power System with High Penetration of Renewable Energy Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The variability and uncertainty of the power outputs from renewable energy sources (RESs) impose higher requirements on the operational flexibility of a power system with RESs integrated. The concept of flexible ramping product (FRP) is thus proposed and has attracted widespread attention in academic and industrial communities, which provides a new alternative for the accommodation of high penetration of renewable energy generation. Given this background, a real-time unit commitment/real-time economic dispatch model considering FRP provided by various flexible resources is proposed. The unit commitment here is with respect to those fast-starting units such as natural gas-fired ones. The unit commitment for conventional thermal units especially coal-fired units is determined in the day-ahead electricity market, and will not be addressed in real time. In the proposed model, the objective is to maximize the social surplus with the integration of multiple types of demand response resources taken into account, while the constraints include unit start-up/shut-down periods and ramping up/down rates in continuous periods. A sample system is next employed to demonstrate the proposed method, and the role of FRP in improving the system flexibility and in enhancing the accommodation capability for RESs is illustrated by some operation scenarios of the sample system. The impact of the prediction confidence of the demanded FRP on the system operational flexibility is also investigated through case studies.

articleTitle: An Optimal Three-Phase Power Control Method of Distribution Network Based on Split-Phase SNOPs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal power flow calculation method of minimum three-phase unbalance of distribution network based on split-phase SNOP breakers. First, a new circuit design of split-phase SNOP breakers is proposed, and its corresponding mathematical modeling is also established. Then, an optimal power flow calculation model of minimum three-phase unbalance of distribution network is developed, based on split-phase SNOP mathematical modeling. The model has 3 objective functions, minimum unbalanced three-phase active load, minimum unbalanced three-phase voltage magnitudes and minimum active power loss of distribution systems. The constraints are included power flow constraints and split-phase SNOP operation constraints. And the relative dominant method is used for transforming dual objectives to one objective, and the immune genetic algorithm is hired for solving. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model is verified by simulation analysis of a practical distribution network with 5 feeders.

articleTitle: Line Loss Association and Prediction Model Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Reducing the line loss of the power grid is a necessary prerequisite for ensuring the quality of the power supply and reducing the power loss of the line. In the past, the research on line loss mainly focused on the analysis of individual influencing factors based on electrical theory, ignoring the fact that the actual line loss is affected by many factors, such as measurement, management, communication, and so on, which limits its practicability. Therefore, this paper proposes a line loss association model based on real grid operation data. The direct numerical relationship between three-phase unbalance, load state, power factor, abnormal communication, meter fault, power consumption and line loss is established by using the method of deep learning, and the characteristics of line loss are analyzed. The results show that the model has certain accuracy and can guide the management planning of power supply enterprises.

articleTitle: Comparison on Three Unscented Transformation Methods for Solving Probabilistic Load Flow
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In general, the UT methods are regarded as the promising tools to solve the probabilistic load flow calculation problem as the correlated random input variables existing in power system can be tackled inherently, with low computational burden and high computational accuracy. In this paper, three different specific UT methods, including traditional UT method with symmetric sampling strategy (SUT), spherical simplex UT (SSUT) and high-order UT (HOUT), are presented and tested on the modified IEEE 118-bus system, under impact of different number of input random variables and diverse correlation levels amongst some of them. Based on the comparison results, it reveals that SUT is able to achieve a good balance between computational speed and accuracy in most cases. Similar conclusion can be drawn by the HOUT method, but it is implied at the price of a considerably higher computational burden. In addition, SSUT merely behaves well in low-dimensional random variables problem.

articleTitle: Knowledge Acquisition for Transformer Condition Assessment Using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique and Decision Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a knowledge acquisition method for transformer condition assessment using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and decision tree algorithm. SMOTE oversampling algorithm is utilized to supplement the minority samples. The transformer condition assessment is a classification process because its results are divided into four classes: normal condition, attentive condition, abnormal condition, and serious condition. Moreover, a decision tree is constructed using C4.5 algorithm to handle this classification problem. Key indicators and rules of transformer condition assessment are derived for the decision tree. The case study is performed on 110kV oil-immersed transformers using inspection and maintenance records. These records are collected from a power distribution company. The results indicate that the proposed method can automatically acquire the knowledge of condition assessment, which is capable for decision support.

articleTitle: Study of Superconducting Fault Current Limiters for MMC-MTDC with HVDC CBs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To minimize the impact of dc faults in modular multilevel converter based multi-terminal high voltage transmission system (MMC-MT-HVDC, MMC-MTDC), HVDC circuit breakers (HVDC CBs) combined with superconducting fault current limiters (SFCLs) was a preferred choice. For MMC-MTDC with HVDC CBs and SFCLs, this paper firstly analyzed the dc fault characteristics based on the equivalent electrical circuit for different operation stages. Then, this paper introduced the basic principle of resistive SFCLs and inductive SFCLs, and their effect in limiting the dc fault current. Based on the main purposes for installing SFCLs, this paper proposed a dc side main circuit parameters selection method for determining the parameters of the smoothing reactor and the SFCLs. The case studies are performed on a ±500 kV 3-ternimal MMC-MTDC system. The time-domain simulation results showed that both the resistive SFCLs and the inductive SFCLs could limit the dc fault current to a reasonable extend by selecting the proper parameters of the smoothing reactor and the SFCLs, and the energy stress on the voltage limiting element of the HVDC CBs is more severe when using the inductive SFCLs.

articleTitle: AGC Strategy for Distributed Energy Storage Aggregator Based on Consensus Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To encourage distributed energy storage systems (ESS) in automatic generation control (AGC), energy storage aggregator (ESA) which aggregates a large number of disordered, autonomously operating, and weakly connected distributed ESS is applied in current power system control area. In this paper, an AGC strategy for ESA based on consensus algorithm is proposed to enable distributed ESS responding to AGC signal. In detail, the strategy picks up the high frequency component from AGC signals for ESA by low-pass filter at the beginning. Furthermore, on the basis of the mathematical model of distributed ESS in frequency regulation, the consensus algorithm is used to allocate the control responsibility to each ESS by considering SoC balance and plug - play function. Also, the consensus algorithm can save computing time and communication cost with strong anti-interference ability. Finally, the promising results of the proposed AGC strategy are simulated by Matlab/Simulink. Those results verify the control strategy can improve the frequency performance of the power system control area, and allocate the control responsibility of ESS accurately.

articleTitle: Situational awareness for dynamic power system based on UKF-driven residual matrix analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: An architecture based on UKF-driven residual matrix analysis is proposed to achieve the situational awareness for dynamic power system in this paper. Firstly, multi-node voltage state estimation of the dynamic power system is achieved by a centralized adaptive UKF in which time-varying noise can be effectively evaluated. Therefore, the spatial-temporal relationship among grid nodes under normal conditions is eliminated and the associated random characteristics is enhanced. On this basis, the effect of abnormal condition can be reflected by the entries of moving-windowed voltage residual matrix, and the associated eigenvalue distribution characteristics will be changed. Furthermore, a situational indicator based on residual covariance transform is proposed to quantify the effect of the abnormal condition, and its awareness performance is derived. Finally, the proposed method is validated based on IEEE-30 bus test case, which shows its applicability to assist with the enhancement of power system reliability.

articleTitle: Research Status and Prospective on Current Transformer Saturation Recognition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Saturation identification of current transformers (CT) has always been one of the most important issues in power system relay protection. At present, the saturation phenomenon of CT is widespread in China. In order to accurately grasp the current research status and future research directions of current transformer saturation identification, the author summarizes and classifies the existing methods of current transformer saturation identification: based on CT physical quantities identification method, based on other physical quantities identification method and based on waveform singularity identification method, respectively, introduces the research principles and characteristics of these methods. The research progress of each method is summarized, and the shortcomings of some methods are pointed out. Finally, several key issues in the future of CT saturation identification are summarized, and prospects for future research are put forward.

articleTitle: Instantaneous-Power-Theory-Based Approach for Electromagnetic Transient Modeling of Loads at Bulk Supply Points
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper develops an approach based on Instantaneous Power Theory (IPT) for electromagnetic transient (EMT) modeling of loads at bulk supply points. The approach is developed because an EMT model can indicate the instantaneous load characteristics with a time step much smaller than the period of the system, which is not applicable to traditional load modeling where only RMS values are concerned. The EMT modeling of loads is to model the instantaneous currents of loads. In the approach, the real and reactive powers of loads are considered as instantaneous powers, and IPT is used to derive the instantaneous currents. The EMT modeling approach is simulated in an equivalent network of a real grid with voltage disturbances and validated with different load models. The load characteristics of all load models in this approach highly match those in traditional load modeling but with a smaller time step than that of traditional load modeling.

articleTitle: A novel fault section location method based on binary global-best harmony search algorithm for electric power distribution systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In response to the demand to improve efficiency and reliability of power system, the growing number of distributed generation (DG) has been implemented in distribution networks, making the networks more complicated. Combined with fault current information collected by feeder terminal unit (FTU) and fault switch function, this paper proposes a binary global-best harmony search algorithm (BGHS) to provide an accurate fault section location method for distribution networks with DG. The proposed algorithm adopts binary coding mode to fit the characteristics of the switch function, and employs the best harmony to perform pitch adjustment that enhances the accuracy and convergence rate. The correctness and feasibility of the algorithm is validated in a test distribution network with DG. The simulation results have shown remarkable accuracy in fault section location. Compared with harmony search (HS) algorithm and genetic algorithm (GA) in terms of number of premature convergences, convergence rate and computation time, the proposed algorithm shows a better performance.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Power Flow Calculation of Offshore Oilfield Power Grid Based on Improved PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: According to the characteristics of offshore oilfield power grid, a nonlinear programming power flow model considering the characteristics of source and load is established, and a power flow solving method based on improved PSO is designed. Firstly, frequency and slip ratio are introduced as flow state variables with voltage amplitude and phase angle, and three characteristic equations of the relationship between rotating load slip ratio, rotating load power, generator power and flow state variables are given, which are applied to the nonlinear programming model of power flow. Then, the improved PSO based on master-slave mode is used to solve the model. Master station divides subgroups and sets optimal solution archives. Slave station uses the Box-Muller Transform to initialize the subgroups and improves the evolution strategy by using individual inferior solution. The rationality of the proposed power flow model and the effectiveness of the algorithm are verified by the case.

articleTitle: Power system transient stability margin assessment using steady-state information
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Transient stability margin assessment provides power grid dispatchers with important criteria for decision-making and preventive control. The computational efficiency of online transient stability margin assessment can be largely improved with the use of steady-state information. In this paper, we propose a novel methodology for online stability margin assessment. A multi-swing based strategy that overcomes the false identification issues of previous methods is firstly illustrated. Based on this improved strategy, a composite neural network is constructed and trained offline to establish the mapping relationship between steady-state characteristics and generator transient stability indices. Finally, the trained neural network is utilized for online transient stability margin assessment. The major advantage of the proposed methodology is that we only use steady-state information in the online assessment process therefore system transient stability margin under worst disturbances can be fast and accurately predicted, providing system dispatchers with adequate time for preventive control. The validity of the proposed methodology is demonstrated in the IEEE 39-bus system.

articleTitle: Chance-Constrained DG Hosting Capacity Assessment With Spatially Correlated Wind Speed
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a distribution network's maximum distributed generation (DG) hosting capacity assessment method considering multivariate dependences among wind speeds in different locations. Our work in this paper is twofold. First, a vine copula model is introduced to capture the high-dimensional dependence structure of wind speed in different locations. Then, to obtain a trade-off between DG curtailment risk and high penetration level, we propose a novel chance-constrained DG hosting capacity assessment model where renewable energy curtailment level is adjustable and predefined. The proposed model and computational method are validated using a set of historical data from China.

articleTitle: Fusion of Multi-time Section Measurements for State Estimation of Power System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the large-scale development and utilization of renewable energy such as wind power, photovoltaics and hydro- power, as well as the gradually increasing scale and complexity of the power grid in China, it is an important implementation to establish a real-time monitoring, analysis and control system (RTMCS) for ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power system. To great extent, the performance of RTMCS depends on the quality of the data which could be available from power system state estimation. In this paper, a data-driven fusion method based on convolutional neural network (CNN) was proposed to enhance the performance of power system state estimation. Firstly, the CNN was trained offline by historical measurements. Then, the real-time measurements were fused and estimated online by the forward calculation function with the neural network. Finally, we took state estimation as an example to test the performance of CNN proposed in this paper. Compared with the typical state estimation method, the simulation results demonstrated that the proposed method presented a higher estimation accuracy with a simpler model.

articleTitle: Operational Benefits Assessment of Demand Response Based on Linearized Consumers Satisfaction Constraints and Stochastic Simulation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The aggregation of flexible resources in demand side demonstrates a great potential to address the challenges brought by wind power integration. In this paper, we presented a probabilistic method to assess the synthetic benefits of demand response (DR) programs for power system operation under wind power uncertainty. First, the price-based DR programs are described through the elaborated modeling of demand-price elasticity and consumers satisfaction. Then, a short-term stochastic simulation method is proposed, where the randomness of wind generation is captured by Latin Hypercube sampling, and a two-stage stochastic program framework is developed to simulate the consumption re-scheduling in response to dynamic electricity tariffs. Moreover, the linearization technique is introduced to convexity the consumers satisfaction constraints, so that the assessment model converts to a computationally friendly mixed integer linear program (MILP). The simulation outcomes yield the DR performance metrics in several aspects, e.g., economics, renewable energy utilization, and reserve capacity adequacy. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which demonstrates the benefits of DR by significantly improving the wind power utilization with a reduced operational cost and guaranteed consumers satisfaction.

articleTitle: Chance-Constrained Shrunken-Primal-Dual Subgradient (CC-SPDS) Approach for Decentralized Electric Vehicle Charging Control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In this paper, we develop a chance-constrained decentralized electric vehicle (EV) charging control framework to achieve "valley-filling" meanwhile meeting individual charging requirements and satisfying distribution network constraints. The control design is formulated as an optimization problem with a stochastic non-separable objective function and globally coupled chance constraints. We propose a novel chance-constrained shrunken-primal-dual subgradient (CC-SPDS) algorithm to support the chance-constrained decentralized control scheme and verify its efficacy and convergence with a representative distribution network model.

articleTitle: State-evaluation & Risk-assessment based Maintenance Resource Allocation Method for Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that the current distribution system have poor real-time performance and unreasonable operation and maintenance resource allocation, a state maintenance decision-making method based on real-time health status evaluation and risk assessment results of distribution equipment is proposed. Firstly, the real-time health index is evaluated based on distribution equipment status assessment result, and the real-time failure rate is calculated based on exponential model. Secondly, the average real-time failure rate of all equipment is calculated by the feeder partition method; the importance of equipment is determined by the loss cost of failure assets, including the cost of users' loss during power outages, the equipment cost and environmental damage cost. Finally, the relative risk cost of each device is calculated based on the risk loss cost of each device. According to the indicator, the operation and maintenance mode and operation and maintenance sequence of different devices are determined, and a differentiated operation and maintenance strategy is formulated. The validity of the proposed model is verified by an example.

articleTitle: A Review on Dynamic Analysis Methods of Power System Frequency
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Frequency is an extremely important operating parameter of power system, and dynamic analysis of power system frequency is the basis for frequency stability analysis and control. Deep study of the dynamic behavior of system frequency and regional frequency can provide sufficient theoretical basis for evaluating the frequency stability of power system and developing frequency protection strategies. This paper expounds the definition and classification of frequency stability, and summarizes characteristics of three dynamic analysis methods of power system frequency: detailed time domain simulation method, single machine equivalent model method and artificial intelligence method and their advantages and disadvantages, providing basis and reference for related researches.

articleTitle: Visualization System Design for Investment and Planning of Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The rapid development of the active distributed network poses big challenge on accurate investment analysis of distributed network. Therefore, a precise investment model is in great demand to help the operator make optimal investment and planning decision. In this paper, a platform of a visualization system for distributed network investment and planning is proposed, on which the operator can accurately compare the performances of the distributed network with differential configuration sets so as to make better planning decision. The key technologies of the visualization system are detailed introduced, including the organization framework, data structure, data interface, graphic elements model, and multi-layer communication mechanism. The proposed platform has been applied in a real distributed network of a province in China, proving its practice and efficiency.

articleTitle: Study of Typical Scenarios of Wind Power Based on Data Dimension Reduction and Affinity Propagation Clustering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As more and more wind farms are connected to the grid, the high fluctuation of wind power has a great impact on the dispatch of the grid. Optimal dispatch model for power systems is a computationally-demanding task by use of wind power time series data with high dimensionality and redundancy, which leads to the time consuming and occupation of storage resources. To deal with this problem, the most common solution is to create typical scenarios for optimization through aggregating the original data set. However, there are no common ways to create accurate and stable scenarios. Therefore a novel approach is proposed based on wavelet entropy piecewise aggregation approximation and affinity propagation clustering in this paper. This method is proved to be valid by the actual output data of a wind farm in a northwestern province of China. The evaluation indexes show that the proposed method has a good aggregation effect and can be efficiently used for creating the typical scenarios for practice in optimal power dispatch.

articleTitle: The Impact of Grid Uncertainties on Optimal Transmission Switching
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Optimal transmission switching is proposed to reduce transmission congestion and optimize the system operational cost. Such switching decisions are usually determined in the day-ahead stage. However, the load and renewable generation forecasts may have significant deviations from the actual values in the next day. Thus, grid uncertainty is a critical factor in the decision-making process of optimal transmission switching. This paper investigates different approaches for optimal transmission switching under uncertainties. Deterministic optimization methods and stochastic programming methods are compared through a series of numerical studies. And the impact of grid uncertainties on optimal transmission switching is analyzed. The numerical analysis on the IEEE-118 bus system shows that the deterministic approaches can perform well when there are only small uncertainties in the grid. However, the stochastic programming approach is more preferable when significant uncertainties exist in the system.

articleTitle: Minimizing Active Power Losses in Electricity Networks Based on Optimal Location of Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The development in battery energy storage (BESS) technology and rapid rise in power demand have urged together adopting the storage system in conventional power plants in order to cope with the additional loads at an optimal cost. This paper presents an optimization strategy to address effective interfacing of BESSs to the grid with the sole objective of minimizing active power losses; however, voltage profile enhancement is targeted as well as a sub task. The methodology is tested based on real-data-based network and loss sensitivity factor approach is used to make best-selected bus to accommodate the BESS such that the associated parameters are maintained optimally. It has been observed that the grid performance improves in terms of power losses because of the local generation of the BESS at the selected bus, which is possesses the highest index of loss sensitivity factor that quantify the severity of a bus performance.

articleTitle: Study on Voltage and Reactive Power Control of 10kV Direct Load Supply of 220kV Transformer Substation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the development of social economy, the demands for electric power are increasing, and the direct load supply on 10kV side of 220kV transformer substation increasingly common. Under such mode, the difficulty in Automatic Voltage Control (AVC) voltage/reactive power control caused by voltage regulating conflict between the 10kV side and the 220kV and 110kV side is also becoming more prominent. In this article, the effect of AVC strategy and combined strategy on the quality of electric energy is discussed; the voltage regulating problems of direct load supply are classified and discussed; the solution for on-line computation of the sensitivity of tapping point voltage regulation, regulating the main transformer unloaded tap position and adjusting the AVC control parameters are put forward, whose application in the voltage and reactive power optimization and improvement of Yibin's power grid is significantly effective.

articleTitle: Pre-Day Coordinated Optimal Control of Large-Scale Electro-thermal Internet Based on The Response of Heating Temperature Demand of Thermal Users
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Energy Internet can promote the comprehensive utilization of energy and the interaction between supply and demand, which has been the focus in academic and industrial fields. How to achieve multi-energy joint planning, time scale coordination and supply-demand balance is the main problem facing energy interconnection. In the integrated energy system of electric-heat interconnection scheduling, the heat demand cannot guarantee real-time balance due to the difference of electricity and heat in dispatching time. To solve this problem, we propose an integrated energy system model that considers the electric-heat time-scale balance and establishes users' comfort index based on fuzzy membership. The increased large-capacity heat storage device can make full use of the advantages of the physical characteristics of the power system and the heat system and improve the large space-time range optimization configuration capability of energy system. According to the balance of total heat in the heat dispatching period, the electric boiler equipment can change the working time to avoid the peak period of electric power. The purpose, we find an optimal time scale of heat dispatched, of this paper is to meet the users' comfortable demand in the most economic way. We take the typical day of a certain area of Liaoning Province in winter as an example. And the simulation results show that the proposed model and scheduling method can improve the economics of the whole system and satisfy the user's comfortable demand.

articleTitle: Economical Operation Optimization of Distribution Network Considering Multiple Adjustment Measures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Due to the strong coupling relationship between active power and reactive power in distribution network, the traditional method of optimizing the active and reactive power cannot make the distribution network operate in the optimal state of economical operation. And the uncertainties of load demand and power of distributed generation bring great challenges to the operation of distribution network. Based on this, a two-stage robust economical operation optimization method for distribution network considering multiple adjustment measures, including on-load tap changer, capacitor banks, static var compensator, electrical storage system and switch reconfiguration, is proposed on the basis of the branch power flow model. And the non-linear power flow constraint is relaxed by second order cone so that the economical operation optimization model is transformed into the mixed integer second order conic programming model to solve effectively. To solve the uncertainties of load demand and power of distributed generation, two-stage robust optimization method is adopted, and the optimal robust operation strategy of each adjustment measure is obtained through the column and constraint generation algorithm. Finally, the validity of the proposed model is verified by IEEE 33 bus system.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow Calculation of Combined Electricity-Heat Power System Based on Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the continuous development of Energy Internet, the power systems and heat systems are beginning to couple and interact. Since the heat system model is more complex and difficult to solve, in order to make the operation of combined system safer, more economical and more reliable, the calculation problem of optimal power flow(OPF) is worth studying. In this paper, to solve the OPF calculation problem of combined electricity-heat power system, an OPF model based on hydraulic model and thermal model of heat system, and DC power flow model of power system was established, and an OPF calculation method based on Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers(ADMM) was proposed to solve the model under the distributed framework. Finally, the correctness, good convergence and strong robustness of this method were proved by comparing with the results of the centralized algorithm and observing its solution process.

articleTitle: Flexible Coordinated Planning of Electricity-gas Integrated Distribution System Considering Demand Side Management
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the rapid development of natural-gas fired units and power-to-gas technology, the interdependency of electricity and natural gas distribution network is deepening day by day. It is of great significance to carry out research on the joint planning of them. On the other hand, demand side management has received more and more attention for realizing the target of peak load shifting and improving the security and economy of the system. Given this background, this paper proposed a coordinated planning method for electricity-gas integrated distribution system considering demand side management. Flexible coefficients are introduced to get a balance between economy and security of the system. Incremental piecewise linearization method and auxiliary variable method are put forward to solve the problem simply and quickly. Case study on an electricity-gas integrated system verified the effectiveness of the proposed planning method.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Handling in Electricity Market Operations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: An electricity market encompasses multiple entities, which undertake the purposes of electricity generation, distribution, as well as regulation in the form of the market authority. There are myriad uncertainties that present themselves in the electricity market, due to factors such as load variability or the inclusion of intermittent sources of generation, which can affect decision-making processes, whether on the part of the market authority or generation companies. These uncertainty factors thus have to be taken into account for the important determination of the electricity pricing and load levels for each time period. This project therefore undertakes the study of the uncertainty-pricing correlation in the electricity market using the chosen approach of stochastic modeling on a MATLAB platform for a better understanding of the effects of uncertainties in the electricity market on electricity pricing.

articleTitle: Research on Comprehensive Assessment System of Park Integrated Energy System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The park integrated energy system is one of the best scenarios to develop multi-energy cooperative utilization and integrated energy service under the background of low-carbon economy. The characteristics of its diverse structure put forward higher demands on the comprehensive construction of the index system. Firstly, considering four kinds of energy forms: electric, heat, cooling, natural gas, from three aspects of technology, economy and environmental protection, the indexes with universal applicability are refined, and the assessment system of park integrated energy system is constructed. Then the weight and scoring function of the index are determined according to the analytic hierarchy process. Finally, the feasibility of the assessment system is verified by taking an park integrated energy system as a case.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Energy Systems Considering Multi-Energy Flow Constraints
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As multi energy-type demands are to be satisfied through physical energy flow networks, multi-energy flow (MEF) is fundamental for analyzing coupled energy flows in integrated energy systems (IES), which is of great significance to the optimal dispatch of integrated energy systems (IES). Therefore, we develop a day-ahead optimal scheduling approach for integrated energy systems (IES) in this paper, aiming at guaranteeing physical feasibility and economic viability of the coordinated scheduling results by considering multi-energy flow constraints. Specifically, based on the models of multiple energy coupling components, electricity network, natural gas network and hydraulic-thermal network, a decomposition-based sequential multi-energy flow calculation method for integrated energy system (IES) is developed to calculate energy flows within coupled electricity, heat, and gas sub-networks. Furthermore, we propose an optimal scheduling method which integrates the decomposed multi-energy flow calculation with the heuristic algorithm to derive day-ahead optimal scheduling results of coupled multi-energy systems. Numerous simulation results are given to illuminate the effectiveness and necessity of considering MEF constraints for the optimal scheduling of IES.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Small Signal Stability Assessment of Large-scale Wind Power Integration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the development of wind power technology, more and more wind generations are integrated into the power system, which will bring new challenges to the power system stability. In this paper, probabilistic method is applied to investigate the small signal stability assessment of large-scale wind power integration, which considering stochastic uncertainty of wind and multiple operation modes of power system. A set of assessment indices which are suitable for large-scale wind power grid connection to analyze the small signal probability stability are proposed, this index system is divided into three categories: the indices related to the characteristic root, damping ratio and distribution factor. Finally, a numerical example is used to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the indices.

articleTitle: An Overview of Planning Technology for Active Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Traditional power grid has become an obstacle for society to promote low-carbon economy due to fossil energy abuse. In order to deal with this crisis, a large amount of distributed energy resource is connected to the distribution network, so as to improve the single energy structure. However, the planning technology of traditional distribution network has been unable to meet the requirements of power supply security and stability after multiple distributed energy resources are connected to the distribution network. Based on the above situation, this paper summarizes the planning technology of active distribution network, describes the difficulties and problems frequently encountered in the planning technology of active distribution network. In the end, this paper presents the summary and outlook for the planning technology of active distribution network.

articleTitle: Research on Power Supply Capability Evaluation and Optimization Method for Distribution Network with Electric Heating Loads
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In order to control air pollution and protect environment, winter clean heating is being vigorously promoted in Northern China. In recent years, the integration of electric heating facilities has a great impact on power supply capability, for which traditional distribution network optimization methods need to be improved. This paper firstly presents multiple typical scenarios of distribution network with electric heating loads, then an evaluation method of power supply capability based on attribute theory is proposed. Lastly, considering seasonal fluctuation of electric heating load, a robust optimization model based on scenario analysis is established, which takes power losses, voltage quality and load balance as multi-objectives to optimize on-off of the switches. Ant colony algorithm based on the Pareto optimal is adopted to solve the model. Taking IEEE 33 nodes distribution system as example, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified, which shows that the economy and power supply capability are balanced with ensuring the node voltage safety.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Modeling and Simulation of CHB Multilevel Converter for EMT-RMS Transients Studies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-scale model of cascaded H-bridge (CHB) converter that is able to simulate slow changing dynamics up to high-frequency switching transients within a same study. By modulating square waveform propagation on transmission line, a semi-analytical switching function model (SFM) is developed, and allows for accelerated simulation of switch-type electromagnetic transients (EMT). Using Fourier series expansion, such SFM is converted to a shifted-frequency dynamic phasor model (DPM) for simulating slow root mean square (RMS) waveforms. Due to the consistent modulation and complex analytical signal processes for different running stages, transitions between the SFM and DPM are smooth within the same run. Case studies involving the CHB energization, cell internal fault, and power oscillation are performed, and the validity of the proposed multi-scale transient model is verified through comparisons of the results with those from the full EMT-type programs.

articleTitle: Cloud-Supported Internet of Things Data Security and Access Control in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The cloud-supported Internet of Things (Cloud-IoT) has been widely used in smart grid. The amount of data related to the power grid is huge and sensitive. In order to improve the security of data storage and achieve fine-grained access control with flexibility, a multi-authorization center and fixed-length ciphertext policy attribute encryption access control scheme with attribute revocation is proposed in this paper. The multi-attribute authority is introduced to generate keys to defend against collusion attack, and partial decryption is delegated to the proxy server to reduce user's computing cost. In addition, user revocation updates and attribute revocation updates are used to improve system flexibility. The security of the scheme is proved by Diffie-Hellman hypothesis, and comparative analysis is carried out. The results show that the scheme effectively improve the speed of encryption and decryption, as well as reduce time cost of the system.

articleTitle: Research on the Key Technologies of Battery Energy Storage Power Station for Plug and Play Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Plug and play (PNP) technology of Battery Energy Storage Power Station (BESPS) based on the emergency support and scale application background of battery energy storage is presented in this paper, and the key to the PNP technology is fully studied. Firstly, PNP technology of BESPS is divided into two dimensions: energy flow level to achieve `plug' goal and information flow level to achieve `play' goal. Then, advanced applications in energy flow level are given, which include conversion control between grid-connected and off-grid, active voltage and frequency support, load peak shifting. The basic principles of establishing BESPS grid-connected communication model and communication mechanism based on information flow are first proposed. The communication interaction method with the example of between Control Center of Power Station (PSCC) and Power Dispatching Center (PDC) is analyzed. the compatibility of BESPS can be improved by researching the basic ways of device interface interoperability, which includes two parts: battery to Energy Storage Unit (ESU), ESU to BESPS. Finally, the BESPS operating between various operation modes are verified by simulation. The research work in this paper has a very positive guiding significance and reference value for the development of enhanced BESPS and solving the problems of large-scale and flexible grid connection of BESPS.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Hybrid AC/DC Distribution Network Based on Two-Stage Robust Optimization Model and Corrective Control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Hybrid AC/DC distribution network (HADDN) will be the development trend of smart grid. This paper presents an optimal operation method for hybrid AC/DC distribution network to achieve safe and economic operation, in the case of uncertain renewable energy (RES) output and load demand. The proposed model is formulated based on a novel two-stage robust model. The first stage of the model optimizes the work states of the on-load tap changers (OLTC), capacitor banks (CBs) and energy storages (ESs) at one cycle. The second stage of the model optimizes the AC/DC converter stations (CSs) output to suppress the overvoltage problem and further reduce the operating cost by using corrective control policy. Furthermore, this paper adopts an ambiguity set to represent uncertainties of RESs and load demand, which makes the model less conservative and also shortens the model solving time. Then, the proposed model can be converted into the mixed integer second-order cone programming (MISCOP) problem, which can be solved by the delayed column-and-constraint generation algorithm. Finally, case study shows that this method can effectively realize safe and economic operation of the HADDN, which is obviously superior to other mainstream methods in reducing operation cost and restraining overvoltage problem.

articleTitle: Asynchronous Distributed Dynamic Economic Dispatch in Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: An increasing number of distributed energy resources (DERs) have penetrated into distribution networks causing great challenges to energy management. The promising solution is distributed optimization where each area optimizes its own subproblems via limited information exchange with neighbors. However, most distributed methods require synchronization which may be impractical due to various local computation ability and communication delay or loss. This paper presents an asynchronous distributed economic dispatch strategy in active distribution networks (ADNs). Firstly, unlike traditional model, active power & reactive power (P-Q) coupling characteristics in ADNs are considered shaping the dispatch more reasonable. Then, an asynchronous fully distributed alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is developed. The proposed method enables each aggregator in ADN optimize their own subproblem through limited information exchange with neighbors in a more flexible and efficient way. Finally, the investigated scheme is validated by numerical tests.

articleTitle: Research on AP Clustering of Weighted Load Index for Demand Response Potential Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Data mining techniques can help utilities to analyze the electricity utilization behavior and make decisions based on massive data from smart meter. In this paper, an innovative Affinity Propagation clustering algorithm is proposed and improved in load curve clustering to analyze demand response potential effectively. First, the feature indices of load curve are extracted to reduce data dimension. In the face of the weakness of subjective weighing, Entropy Weighting is introduced to objectively determine the weight of load feature indices. Then, Preference parameter of AP clustering algorithm is adjusted by local search mechanism to improve the similarity calculation, and the convergence of clustering result is ameliorated by DB index. Based on the clustering result, the feature indices are combined to analyze the demand response potential of customer. Case studies show that the proposed algorithm has good performance in both the clustering efficiency and effect, and the extracted features are beneficial to consumption behavior analysis.

articleTitle: A Corrective Control Approach For Combined Heat And Power System integrated with Multiple Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The integrated Energy System (IES) becomes very important nowadays, however, the coupling between multiple energy systems will bring new challenges to the security control of the IES, such as combined heat and power (CHP) system. The corrective control means that the operations can be adjusted after contingency happens to eliminate the constraints violation in the contingency state such as the transmission outage or generator outage. This paper proposes a corrective control approach for CHP system integrated with the energy storage system based on security constrained economic dispatch (SCED) model. Case studies based on the IEEE 9-bus CHP system are presented to verify the method. The case result shows that the energy storage device can solve the ramping of the unit's output adjustment well. The corrective control method is more scientific and economical.

articleTitle: Modular Distribution Network Reliability Analysis and Comprehensive Evaluation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Aiming at the requirement of high reliability and lean planning for urban medium-voltage distribution network, modularization concept, reliability analysis and comprehensive evaluation methods are proposed. Modular distribution network based on station, room, line and cable is explained. The reliability calculation method based on "component-submodule-module", considering multi-outage and inter-module transfer is proposed. The comprehensive evaluation model of modular distribution network is established in multi-dimension.
